parts.t: North Surrey townhomes are strata homes in complexes spread across Guildford, Whalley, Fraser Heights and Cedar Hills, with a handful in the other sub-areas. Each complex runs under its own bylaws and budget, so two units that look alike can come with very different paperwork. Strata fees also vary with what they cover, since one complex may pay for gas or hot water and another very little, so compare the Form B and budget side by side. Written by
Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®

For townhome buyers weighing Guildford, Whalley and the rest of North Surrey, I read the strata plan, bylaws and repair records with you before you firm up. I've been a REALTOR® since 2015 and I'm in the top 1% of Fraser Valley REALTORS®. I have more than $500M in sales.
Paragon, the MLS® system local REALTORS® use, treats North Surrey as one area made up of eight sub-areas.
Guildford
Guildford
has more townhome complexes than any other part of North Surrey. Many sit near Guildford Exchange, where the R1 RapidBus starts its run along 104 Avenue to Surrey Central Station.
Whalley
Whalley
has a large share too, from older complexes on side streets to newer ones near King George Boulevard. Some are a reasonable walk from Gateway, Surrey Central or King George SkyTrain stations.
Fraser Heights

is mostly detached streets, with a smaller group of complexes between the Fraser River and Highway 1. It has no SkyTrain station and sits farther from the Expo Line than Whalley or Guildford, so most trips start with buses 337 or 338 to Guildford Exchange or a drive to Highway 1.
Cedar Hills
, near Robson Park on 100 Avenue, has a few complexes mixed in among its houses.
A strata is created when a developer files a strata plan at the Land Title Office. Owners hold their own strata lots, and together, as the strata corporation, they own the common property.

blocks.text: Conventional strata vs bare land strata

parts.t: Most townhome complexes are conventional stratas. The strata plan defines each lot by the building's walls, floors and ceilings, and grounds, driveways and roofs are usually shared. Under the Standard Bylaws, the strata corporation must repair the structure and exterior of the building, the exterior doors and windows, and fences that enclose yards and patios.

In a bare land strata, lot lines are drawn by survey markers instead. The plan usually doesn't show the homes at all, and common property is often limited to internal roads, utilities and shared facilities. If the plan shows outlines of individual homes, the Province suggests it may not be bare land.

A townhome's yard, patio or parking pad is often limited common property. That means it's shared property set aside for one unit. Under the Standard Bylaws, the owner with the use of it handles routine upkeep, while the strata covers less frequent work and the items listed above.

blocks.text: Records to read before you buy

parts.t: The strata must provide a Form B within 7 days of a request. It shows the monthly strata fee, any amount owing on the unit, approved special levies and the contingency reserve fund balance.

This report reviews the complex's common assets and estimates what they'll cost to repair and replace over 30 years. For townhomes, think roofs, siding, decks and paving. Stratas with five or more lots need one on a five-year cycle.
The Standard Bylaws apply unless the developer or owners have filed different ones at the Land Title Office. Ask for the full filed set and the current rules.

blocks.text: How I help North Surrey townhome buyers

parts.t: I pull the strata plan first, so we know whether a complex is conventional or bare land and which yard, patio and parking areas belong to the unit. Then I read the depreciation report against the Form B. If the report says roofs or siding are due soon and the reserve looks thin, we ask how the strata plans to pay before you commit.
I also check the filed bylaws for pet limits and rules on changing a patio or fence. If you're working to a budget across the whole city, my

1. Where are most North Surrey townhomes?
Guildford and Whalley hold most of the townhome complexes in North Surrey. Fraser Heights and Cedar Hills have smaller groups, and the other sub-areas have only a few.
2. Is every townhome a strata property?
Most are, but not all. A townhouse in a strata complex can look exactly like a row house that isn't strata-titled, so check the title and the strata plan.
3. What is a bare land strata?

It's a strata plan where lot lines are set by survey markers instead of a building's walls, floors and ceilings. The owner usually looks after the home, and common property is often limited to roads, utilities and shared facilities.
4. Who fixes the roof and siding in a conventional strata?

Under the Standard Bylaws, the strata corporation repairs the structure and exterior of the building, including exterior doors, windows and fences around yards. The complex's own filed bylaws can change that split.
5. Does a townhome complex need a depreciation report?
In BC, a strata with five or more lots must get one on a five-year cycle. It covers the roof, siding, paving and other common assets over 30 years.
6. Where do I find a complex's bylaws?
The Standard Bylaws apply unless the strata has filed different bylaws at the Land Title Office. Ask for the full filed set, plus any rules, with the Form B.
7. Does this page show condos or houses?
No. It shows townhouses across North Surrey only. Apartments and detached homes each have their own North Surrey page.
